# Fixtures

## Our profile

`slot_data_fixture.json` is GENERATED by the apworld pytest
`worlds/eldenring/tests/test_slot_data_fixture.py` (fixed seed 1706) and consumed by
`../slot_data_fixture.rs`. Do not hand-edit; re-run the pytest to refresh. Absent fixture =>
the Rust test soft-skips with a loud line.

## Bedrock profile (foreign apworld)

`slot_data_bedrock.json`, `slot_data_bedrock_items.json` and `shoplineup_flags.json` back the
Bedrock-profile contract tests. They are RECORDED, not generated by our CI, and are absent-fatal
(unlike our own fixture): if they go missing the Bedrock path has no coverage, and the tests say
so loudly rather than skipping.

Consumed by:

- `../slot_data_bedrock.rs` (er-logic: options / version gate / item maps / the baked
  `region_lock` table)
- `crates/eldenring-archipelago/src/bedrock_fixture_test.rs` (the matt key resolver, the foreign
  `goal` key, `region::parse` + the baked fallback). It lives in `src/` because that crate is
  `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` with private modules, so an integration test cannot reach them.

### What produced them

| file | source |
| --- | --- |
| `slot_data_bedrock.json` | slot_data for player 1 of a seed generated from fswap/Archipelago branch `er` @ `2c25448` ("better shard option", 2026-09-06) on Archipelago 0.6.7 |
| `slot_data_bedrock_items.json` | the sorted set of that seed's own item NAMES (from the multidata datapackage) -- the client learns these over the network, and `derive_region_locks` is driven by them |
| `shoplineup_flags.json` | byte copy of `greenfield/eldenring/shoplineup_flags.json` in the world repo (generated there by `tools/gen_shoplineup_flags.py`); the client ships this table at runtime, so the test loads the real one |

Seed options (everything else default):

```yaml
name: BedrockLock
game: EldenRing
EldenRing:
  progression_balancing: 50
  accessibility: full
  world_logic: region_lock
  enable_dlc: true
  enable_tarnished_pack: true
  goal: [Final Boss, DLC Final Boss]
```

`world_logic: region_lock` is deliberate: it is the roll that mints "<Region> Lock" items, and it
is the proof that Bedrock's apworld emits region locks with NO region geometry in slot_data
(`areaLockFlags` and `regionOpenFlags` are both absent), which is the only reason
`region::prepare_baked_fallback` exists. An `open_world` roll of the same options was also
generated and measured: every parser-relevant table was identical, only `options.world_logic`
differed, so only the region-lock seed is recorded.

### How to refresh when Bedrock's world moves

1. `git clone --depth 1 -b 0.6.7 https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago` (the pin is the
   `.ap-version` in the world repo) into a scratch directory. Do NOT reuse the world repo's
   `.ap-test` -- its `worlds/eldenring` is ours, and the Bedrock world must ALSO be named
   `eldenring` for its own relative imports to resolve.
2. Copy fswap/Archipelago branch `er`'s `worlds/eldenring` into that checkout's `worlds/`.
3. Write the yaml above into a `Players/` directory of its own (the world's `force_region_lock`
   host setting refuses `open_world` in a multi-player generation; one player per run sidesteps
   it).
4. `SKIP_REQUIREMENTS_UPDATE=1 AP_NONINTERACTIVE=1 python Generate.py --player_files_path Players
   --outputpath out --seed 1`
5. The `.archipelago` inside the output zip is a 1-byte header followed by a zlib-compressed
   pickle; `Utils.restricted_loads(zlib.decompress(raw[1:]))["slot_data"][1]` is the fixture. The
   item names come from the same structure: invert
   `datapackage["EldenRing"]["item_name_to_id"]` over every `locations` entry whose receiving
   player is 1, plus `precollected_items[1]`.
6. Re-run `cargo test -p er-logic --test slot_data_bedrock` and
   `cargo test -p eldenring-archipelago bedrock`. The asserted counts WILL move. Read the delta
   before updating them -- a drop in resolved locations or in DISTINCT shop stock flags is a
   regression in our parsers, not a fixture refresh.
7. Update the commit and options recorded above.

er-archipelago issue #1463 makes a world declare its own `profile` key. Once that lands, this
fixture should carry `profile: bedrock`, and the client's profile-SELECTION test belongs here
alongside the parser tests. Do not implement #1463 from this side; re-record the fixture once the
key exists, then assert the selection instead of inferring the profile from which keys are absent.
